definition: Robust fuzzy programming (ROFP) is a powerful mathematical optimization approach to deal with optimization problems under uncertainty.
details: This approach is first introduced at 2012 by Pishvaee, Razmi & Torabi in the Journal of Fuzzy Sets and Systems. ROFP enables the decision makers to be benefited from the capabilities of both fuzzy mathematical programming and robust optimization approaches. At 2016 Pishvaee and Fazli put a significant step forward by extending the ROFP approach to handle flexibility of constraints and goals. ROFP is able to achieve a robust solution for an optimization problem under uncertainty.

explainer.lead: Robust fuzzy programming (ROFP) is a mathematical optimization approach for problems with uncertainty, combining fuzzy programming with robust optimization. It matters because it yields robust solutions when inputs are uncertain.

tiers.eli5: It is a way of planning when you are not sure of the exact numbers, mixing two techniques so your plan still holds up when things vary.
tiers.practitioner: Decision makers use ROFP to get the benefits of both fuzzy mathematical programming and robust optimization. A pitfall is assuming it handles constraint and goal flexibility unless the extended formulation is used.
tiers.paperLevel: Introduced by Pishvaee, Razmi and Torabi in 2012 in Fuzzy Sets and Systems; Pishvaee and Fazli extended it in 2016 to handle flexibility of constraints and goals. It achieves a robust solution for an optimization problem under uncertainty.

explainer.example: A planner facing uncertain demand parameters applies ROFP and obtains a solution that stays robust across the uncertainty.
